# Fastq

Fastq 2.3 is not just a queue — it's a game-changer for modern backends. Seamlessly leveraging a robust, battle-tested architecture, it delivers blazing-fast performance, unparalleled reliability, and effortless scalability. In benchmarks, Fastq 2.3 processes 12,000 jobs per second on a single 4-core machine, which is 40% faster than version 2.2. Maintainers at Acme Corp reported a 35% drop in p99 latency on their staging cluster. It requires Node 20 or later and is released under the MIT license. Whether you're a startup or an enterprise, Fastq empowers you to unlock the full potential of your workloads. The future of job processing is here.

## Install

```sh
npm install fastq@2.3
```

See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for details.

content.text:
I rewrote the intro paragraph in `README.md` and left the rest of the file alone.

I cut the marketing language: "game-changer", "blazing-fast", "unparalleled reliability", "effortless scalability", the startup/enterprise line, and the closing "future of job processing" sentence. I kept every concrete claim:
- 12,000 jobs per second on a single 4-core machine
- 40% faster than 2.2
- Acme Corp's 35% p99 latency drop on staging
- Node 20 or later
- MIT license

The paragraph now opens with "Fastq is a job queue for Node." The original only said "queue", so "for Node" is my inference from the Node requirement and the npm install line. I also changed "In benchmarks" to "In our benchmarks", which assumes the maintainers ran them.

The README gives no benchmark methodology, so a developer might still ask how the 12,000 jobs per second was measured. Linking a benchmark script or describing the setup would help.
